headline: Defense start-up Anduril will invest $3.7 billion in a new Maryland shipyard for submarine parts, and the US Navy has given it a contract worth up to $2.9 billion.
score_reason: New, company-announced; the plant does not yet exist.
importance_line: US taxpayers pay for the submarine parts only as Anduril delivers them, with the company carrying most of the risk, but the plant is not due to run until the end of the decade.
summary: Military Times reports that Anduril, a defence start-up best known for drones and autonomous systems, said on 6 Oct 2026 it will invest $3.7 billion in a new Baltimore County plant to build parts for the Navy's Virginia-class nuclear-powered attack submarines, due to run by the end of the decade with 3,100 direct jobs. The Navy contract for up to $2.9 billion pays according to production results, with Anduril carrying most of the risk; together the two are worth up to $6.6 billion, according to the company.
notes: The Tech Buzz piece (pool link) was not used: it is unsourced and its claims conflict with Military Times. Luckey's Pentagon advisory role is in CNBC's headline only, so left out of the entry.
